newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Airlines to buy six 50-seater aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Indian Airlines to buy six 50-seater aircraft.

text.p: Indian Airlines, the nation's largest domestic air carrier, is planning to buy six 50-seater planes, Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim said on Friday.
"Six 50-seater aircrafts will be purchased," Ibrahim told a news conference in the Indian capital.
A special committee has short-listed three aircraft and a decision to buy will be taken soon, he said. The three aircraft are the ATR-42, Saab-2000 and Dash-8, airline officials said.
The 50-seater aircraft will be used on sectors where the passenger load is lighter, Ibrahim said, adding that this would allow the airline to use larger planes on high-demand routes.
The Indian government subsidises passenger air fares on many routes, mainly in less-developed regions where rail and road transport facilities are not adequate.
Officials said the 50-seater aircraft would be flown on these routes.
But the state-owned airline would like to charge economy fares on these aircraft. A decision has to be taken after talks with the government, Aviation Ministry officials said.
